target: The Claude Code agent configuration of the repo at <REPO>: .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json if present, .mcp.json, hooks and the scripts they run, and any CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md instructions that grant or restrict tools.
context: Read-only review of how much an agent working in this repo is allowed to do, and whether that matches what the repo needs.
rules: Read-only. Never run the hooks or MCP servers; read their code. Don't print secret values: name the setting, not the value.

groups.prompt: Every permission rule (allow, ask, deny), the default mode and additionalDirectories: what each allows, checked against the Claude Code settings docs (context7). Flag broad rules such as Bash(*), Read(**) outside the repo, or bypass modes.
Every hook: its event, matcher, the command it runs, and what that command can do. Flag hooks that run network calls, write outside the repo, or could be steered by tool input.
Every MCP server: transport, where its credentials come from (header, URL, env, headersHelper), which tools it exposes, and whether any key appears in plain text in config.
Tabulate what an agent can do here without a prompt: tools, paths, commands and network, as a least-privilege inventory.

logic.prompt: Do the permissions match what the repo's workflows and CLAUDE.md actually need? Name anything granted but unused.

attacks.prompt: Target: the claim that this configuration is least-privilege. Argue against it: prompt injection through fetched or repo content reaching an allowed tool, compound Bash commands, reads of secrets via allowed tools, and hooks as an escalation path.
